My kok is terug, hier is wat hy gekry het:

**The dish**
Soet hoenderkerrie (sweet chicken curry), with rice and peas. The curry already uses chicken, so I've kept it as chicken thighs, the cut that suits a curry best. Nothing else changes, and the total is still about R361.

**Recipe**

![Soet hoenderkerrie – gewone kerrie, huiskerrie](https://marindakook.co.za/wp-content/uploads/2017/10/featured-soet-hoenderkerrie-blog-028.jpg)

Serves 2 · about 1 hour

1. Cut 1 kg chicken thighs into bite-sized pieces. Boneless thighs cut small cook fastest.
2. Slice the onion into rings and fry in the oil until glassy. Add the crushed garlic clove and fry briefly. Add the chicken and brown it lightly.
3. Peel the potatoes, cut them into quarters and add them to the pot.
4. Dissolve the stock cube in 375 ml warm water. Add it to the pot with the bay leaf, curry powder, apricot jam, vinegar, sugar, borrie, salt and pepper.
5. Simmer covered for 25–30 minutes, until the chicken is tender and the potatoes are soft.
6. To thicken, mix the cornflour with 40 ml cold water into a paste, stir it in and simmer for 5 minutes.
7. Serve with the rice and peas.

Link: https://marindakook.co.za/soet-hoenderkerrie-gewone-kerrie-huiskerrie/

| Chicken stock cube | 1 cube | chicken stock cubes 6 pack | ± R18 |
| Dried bay leaf | 1 leaf | dried bay leaves 10 g | ± R12 |
| Curry powder | 30 ml (about 20 g) | curry powder 100 g | ± R35 |
| Apricot jam | 30 ml | apricot jam 250 g | ± R30 |
| White vinegar | 30 ml | white vinegar 750 ml | ± R18 |
| Sugar | 30 ml | white sugar 1 kg | ± R28 |
| Borrie | 15 ml | borrie 100 g | ± R25 |
| Cornflour (maizena) | 5 ml | cornflour 200 g | ± R22 |
| Rice | 150 g (dry) | rice 1 kg | ± R30 |
| Frozen peas | 150 g | frozen peas 500 g | ± R35 |
| **Total** | | | **± R361** |

From the pantry: cooking oil, salt and pepper.

Prices are estimates, not checked at a shop.

**Unsure**

| What | Why |
|---|---|
| Meat swap | The curry already uses chicken thighs, so nothing changed. If you meant a different meat (beef or lamb, for example), say so and I'll redo the list. |
| All prices | Estimates: no shop's prices are looked up for now. Pack prices are for full packs, so leftovers add to the cost. |
| Cooking time | The recipe's 60-minute simmer is for bone-in pieces. I've adapted it to boneless thighs cut small (25–30 minutes), so the whole meal fits about an hour. |
| Borrie | I couldn't confirm what borrie is or which product to buy. Ask at the shop, or leave it out; the curry will be a little different. |
| Recipe scale | The source recipe is for a whole chicken, serving more people. I halved it for two. |
| Branch | You didn't give a suburb, so I found the two Pick n Pay branches in Pretoria nearest the centre. Neither is confirmed as nearest to you. |

So the short answer: the curry was already chicken, so the list is the same as before. If you had something else in mind, like beef or lamb, tell me and I'll redo it.
